He began to mock him. To insult him. And then came Duskendale. A minor lord of a port town refused to pay his taxes. Aerys went to Duskendale in person, to settle it. The lord seized him, and held the king of the Seven Kingdoms prisoner for half a year. Ser Barristan Selmy finally slipped into the town alone and brought him out. But the man who came out was not the man who went in. Afterwards, Aerys would not leave the Red Keep. He trusted no one.
c23: He would not let a blade come near him, so he stopped cutting his hair and his nails. They grew long, tangled and yellow. And he found a new obsession. Fire. He surrounded himself with pyromancers, the alchemists of the wildfire guild, and the whole court lived in terror of the flames. In the two hundred and eighty-first year, a great tourney was held at Harrenhal. Prince Rhaegar won it. And as the champion, he was meant to crown a lady as queen of love and beauty. Everyone expected him to crown his wife, Elia Martell of Dorne. Instead, he rode past her, and laid a crown of blue winter roses in the lap of Lyanna Stark. In the first book, Ned Stark remembers that moment as the moment all the smiles died. A year later, Rhaegar and Lyanna disappeared together. Robert's great warhammer broke Rhaegar's breastplate, and Rhaegar fell in the river. Its rubies scattered into the water, and men dove for them for years afterward. And the Lannister army poured into the city.
c24: And in the throne room, a young knight of the Kingsguard named Jaime Lannister heard the king chanting the same words, over and over. Burn them all. c25: And then Viserys sold Daenerys too. He married her to a Dothraki warlord, Khal Drogo, in exchange for an army that never came. In the books that followed, Daenerys crossed the red waste, freed the slaves of Astapor, Yunkai and Meereen, and ruled Meereen as its queen, trying, and often failing, to make a broken city work. At the end of the fifth book, Drogon carries her out of a fighting pit and far into the Dothraki Sea. That is where her story stops. For now. But she is not the only Targaryen left in the books. Old Maester Aemon, Egg's brother, the last Targaryen at the Wall, dies at sea on his way to Oldtown, murmuring about dragons, and about her. In his last moments, he calls for his little brother. Egg. I dreamed that I was old.
c26: In the fifth book, a young man called Griff appears in Essos, claiming to be Rhaegar's son, Aegon, saved from the sack as a baby. And the army marching behind him is the Golden Company. The sellswords founded by Bittersteel, the Blackfyre exile. Many readers suspect he is not who he claims to be. That he may be a Blackfyre, at last coming home. The books have not said. In the show, it is confirmed: Jon is the son of Rhaegar and Lyanna, and his true name is Aegon Targaryen. In the books, it is one of the most famous theories ever written about a story that has not finished yet. The hints are all there. Promise me, Ned. The show gave the dynasty an ending. Daenerys burned King's Landing, Jon killed her, and Drogon melted the Iron Throne. In the books, that ending has not been written. The Winds of Winter is still unpublished.
